- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at +2% above prior peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral/negative.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model underestimates — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to compensate for mean reversion bias.
- Model exhibits strong lag in reacting to sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns positive after 3–5 days, adjust forecast upward by 0.3–0.8% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility — smooth out forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ prices unless sentiment strongly signals reversal.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “+0.67” followed by “-0.00” or “0.33”, model tends to overreact — apply a 0.5–1.0% downward correction to prevent overcorrection.
